💬 Assistant Response\n\nI have completed the implementation of the bidirectional interactive mode for issue #817. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:\n\n## Summary\n\n**Pull Request:** https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/843\n\n### Implementation Details\n\n1. **New `--bidirectional-interactive` CLI Option**: Added to both `solve` and `hive` commands. This option enables monitoring of PR comments during Claude execution for real-time user feedback.\n\n2. **New Library `src/bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs`** containing:\n   - `createBidirectionalHandler()` - Factory function for feedback queue management\n   - `isSystemComment()` - Filters out system-generated comments (from interactive mode itself)\n   - `formatFeedbackForClaude()` - Formats feedback in Claude's stream-json format\n   - Comment monitoring with configurable poll interval (default: 15 seconds)\n\n3. **Integration in `src/claude.lib.mjs`**:\n   - Creates and starts bidirectional handler when enabled\n   - Initializes with existing comments to only process NEW comments\n   - Reports collected feedback at end of execution\n   - Returns queued feedback in execution result\n\n4. **Comprehensive Unit Tests**: 27 passing test cases in `tests/test-bidirectional-interactive.mjs`\n\n### How It Works\n\nWhen `--bidirectional-interactive` is enabled:\n1. The system monitors PR comments during Claude execution\n2. User comments (not system-generated) are queued as feedback\n3. At the end of execution, any collected feedback is reported\n4. The challenge is that the current implementation uses `command-stream` to execute Claude with a simple stdin (the initial prompt). For bidirectional mode, we need to be able to write additional messages to stdin during execution.\\n\\nLooking at the code, I see that currently:\\n1. When not resuming, it passes `stdin: prompt` directly\\n2. The command streams output but stdin is a one-shot operation\\n\\nFor true bidirectional mode, we would need to:\\n1. Use `spawn` directly instead of command-stream\\n2. Keep stdin open and writable\\n3. Write feedback messages when available\\n\\nHowever, looking at my earlier experiments, I realized that Claude CLI in `-p` (print) mode exits after processing one user message. };\n  }\n  const totalCost = new Decimal(breakdown.input.cost).plus(breakdown.cacheWrite.cost).plus(breakdown.cacheRead.cost).plus(breakdown.output.cost).toNumber();\n  if (includeBreakdown) {\n million = new Decimal(1000000);\n  const breakdown = {\n    input: { tokens: 0, costPerMillion: 0, cost: 0 },\n    cacheWrite: { tokens: 0, costPerMillion: 0, cost: 0 },\n    cacheRead: { tokens: 0, };\n  }\n  const totalCost = new Decimal(breakdown.input.cost).plus(breakdown.cacheWrite.cost).plus(breakdown.cacheRead.cost).plus(breakdown.output.cost).toNumber();\n  if (includeBreakdown) {\n Only supported for --tool claude.',\n      default: false\n    })\n    .parserConfiguration({\n      'boolean-negation': true,\n    })\n    // Use yargs built-in strict mode to reject unrecognized options\n    // This prevents issues like #453 and #482 where unknown options are silently ignored\n    .strict()\n    .help('h')\n    .alias('h', 'help');\n\n  return config;\n};\n\n// Parse command line arguments - now needs yargs and hideBin passed in\nexport const parseArguments = async (yargs, hideBin) => {\n  const rawArgs = hideBin(process.argv);\n\n  // Issue #1092: Detect malformed flag patterns BEFORE yargs parsing\n  // This catches cases like \"-- model\" which yargs silently treats as positional arguments\n  const malformedResult = detectMalformedFlags(rawArgs);\n  if (malformedResult.malformed.length > 0) {\n    const error = new Error(malformedResult.errors.join('\\n'));\n    error.name = 'MalformedArgumentError';\n    throw error;\n  }\n\n  // Use .parse() instead of .argv to ensure .strict() mode works correctly\n  // When you call yargs(args) and use .argv, strict mode doesn't trigger\n  // See: https://github.com/yargs/yargs/issues - .strict() only works with .parse()\n\n  let argv;\n  let yargsInstance;\n  try {\n    // Suppress stderr output from yargs during parsing to prevent validation errors from appearing\n    // This prevents \"YError: Not enough arguments\" from polluting stderr (issue #583)\n    // Save the original stderr.write\n    const originalStderrWrite = process.stderr.write;\n    const stderrBuffer = [];\n\n    // Temporarily override stderr.write to capture output\n    process.stderr.write = function (chunk, encoding, callback) {\n      stderrBuffer.push(chunk.toString());\n      // Call the callback if provided (for compatibility)\n      if (typeof encoding === 'function') {\n        encoding();\n      } else if (typeof callback === 'function') {\n        callback();\n      }\n      return true;\n    };\n\n    try {\n      yargsInstance = createYargsConfig(yargs());\n      argv = await yargsInstance.parse(rawArgs);\n    } finally {\n      // Always restore stderr.write\n      process.stderr.write = originalStderrWrite;\n\n      // In verbose mode, show what was captured from stderr (for debugging)\n      if (global.verboseMode && stderrBuffer.length > 0) {\n        const captured = stderrBuffer.join('');\n        if (captured.trim()) {\n          console.error('[Suppressed yargs stderr]:', captured);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    // Yargs throws errors for validation issues\n    // If the error is about unknown arguments (strict mode), enhance it with suggestions\n    // Check if this error has already been enhanced to avoid re-processing\n    if (error.message && /Unknown argument/.test(error.message) && !error._enhanced) {\n      try {\n        // Enhance the error message with helpful suggestions\n        // Use the yargsInstance we already created, or create a new one if needed\n        const yargsWithConfig = yargsInstance || createYargsConfig(yargs());\n        const enhancedMessage = enhanceErrorMessage(error.message, yargsWithConfig);\n        const enhancedError = new Error(enhancedMessage);\n        enhancedError.name = error.name;\n        enhancedError._enhanced = true; // Mark as enhanced to prevent re-processing\n        throw enhancedError;\n      } catch (enhanceErr) {\n        // If enhancing fails, just throw the original error\n        if (global.verboseMode) {\n          console.error('[VERBOSE] Failed to enhance error message:', enhanceErr.message);\n        }\n        // If the enhance error itself is already enhanced, throw it\n        if (enhanceErr._enhanced) {\n          throw enhanceErr;\n        }\n        throw error;\n      }\n    }\n    // For other validation errors, show a warning in verbose mode\n    if (error.message && global.verboseMode) {\n      console.error('Yargs parsing warning:', error.message);\n    }\n    // Try to get the argv even with the error\n    argv = error.argv || {};\n  }\n\n  // Post-processing: Fix model default for opencode and codex tools\n  // Yargs doesn't properly handle dynamic defaults based on other arguments,\n  // so we need to handle this manually after parsing\n  const modelExplicitlyProvided = rawArgs.includes('--model') || rawArgs.includes('-m') || rawArgs.includes('--worker-model');\n  const planModelExplicitlyProvided = rawArgs.includes('--plan-model');\n\n  // --plan flag expansion (Issue #1223)\n  // When --plan is set, it acts as a shortcut for --plan-model opus --worker-model sonnet\n  // Explicit --plan-model and --model/--worker-model values take precedence\n  if (argv && argv.plan) {\n    if (!planModelExplicitlyProvided) {\n      argv.planModel = 'opus';\n    }\n    if (!modelExplicitlyProvided) {\n      argv.model = 'sonnet';\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Normalize alias flags: legacy --skip-tool-check and --skip-claude-check behave like --skip-tool-connection-check\n  if (argv) {\n    // Support deprecated flags\n    if (argv.skipToolCheck || argv.skipClaudeCheck) {\n      argv.skipToolConnectionCheck = true;\n    }\n    // Support negated deprecated flag: --no-tool-check becomes --no-tool-connection-check\n    if (argv.toolCheck === false) {\n      argv.toolConnectionCheck = false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // --finalize normalization\n  // Issue #1383: When finalize is enabled (as boolean or number), normalize to iteration count\n  // NOTE: promptEnsureAllRequirementsAreMet is NOT set here — it is only enabled during\n  // the finalize cycle iterations themselves (not the first regular worker model run)\n  if (argv && argv.finalize) {\n    // Normalize: if passed as boolean true (flag without value), treat as 1 iteration\n    if (argv.finalize === true) {\n      argv.finalize = 1;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // --working-session-live-progress normalization\n  // When passed as --working-session-live-progress (no value), yargs gives true for string type\n  // Normalize: true → \"comment\", validate known values\n  if (argv && Monitors GitHub PR comments for new user feedback\n * - Queues feedback messages for injection into Claude's stdin\n * - Works with Claude CLI's --input-format stream-json mode\n * - Filters out system-generated comments (from interactive mode itself)\n *\n * Usage:\n *   const { createBidirectionalHandler } = await import('./bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs');\n *   const handler = createBidirectionalHandler({ owner, repo, prNumber, $ });\n *   await handler.startMonitoring();\n *   // Later...\n *   const feedback = handler.getQueuedFeedback();\n *\n * @module bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs\n * @experimental\n */\n\n// Configuration constants\nconst CONFIG = {\n  // Minimum time between comment checks to avoid rate limiting (in ms)\n  MIN_POLL_INTERVAL: 10000,\n  // Default poll interval (in ms)\n  DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL: 15000,\n  // Maximum queued feedback messages\n  MAX_QUEUE_SIZE: 50,\n  // Signature to identify system-generated comments\n  SYSTEM_COMMENT_SIGNATURES: [\n    '## 🚀 Session Started',\n    '## 💬 Assistant Response',\n    '## 💻 Tool: ',\n    '## 📝 Tool: ',\n    '## 📖 Tool: ',\n    '## ✏️ Tool: ',\n    '## 🔍 Tool: ',\n    '## 🔎 Tool: ',\n    '## 🌐 Tool: ',\n    '## 📋 Tool: ',\n    '## 🎯 Tool: ',\n    '## 📓 Tool: ',\n    '## 🔧 Tool: ',\n    '## ✅ Tool Result:',\n    '## ❌ Tool Result:',\n    '## ✅ Session Complete',\n    '## ❌ Session Failed',\n    '## ❓ Unrecognized Event:',\n    '📄 Raw JSON',\n    '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]',\n    '🤖 AI-Powered Solution Draft',\n    '*This PR was created automatically by the AI issue solver*'\n  ]\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a comment body is system-generated (from interactive mode)\n *\n * @param {string} body - Monitors GitHub PR comments for new user feedback\n * - Queues feedback messages for injection into Claude's stdin\n * - Works with Claude CLI's --input-format stream-json mode\n * - Filters out system-generated comments (from interactive mode itself)\n *\n * Usage:\n *   const { createBidirectionalHandler } = await import('./bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs');\n *   const handler = createBidirectionalHandler({ owner, repo, prNumber, $ });\n *   await handler.startMonitoring();\n *   // Later...\n *   const feedback = handler.getQueuedFeedback();\n *\n * @module bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs\n * @experimental\n */\n\n// Configuration constants\nconst CONFIG = {\n  // Minimum time between comment checks to avoid rate limiting (in ms)\n  MIN_POLL_INTERVAL: 10000,\n  // Default poll interval (in ms)\n  DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL: 15000,\n  // Maximum queued feedback messages\n  MAX_QUEUE_SIZE: 50,\n  // Signature to identify system-generated comments\n  SYSTEM_COMMENT_SIGNATURES: [\n    '## 🚀 Session Started',\n    '## 💬 Assistant Response',\n    '## 💻 Tool: ',\n    '## 📝 Tool: ',\n    '## 📖 Tool: ',\n    '## ✏️ Tool: ',\n    '## 🔍 Tool: ',\n    '## 🔎 Tool: ',\n    '## 🌐 Tool: ',\n    '## 📋 Tool: ',\n    '## 🎯 Tool: ',\n    '## 📓 Tool: ',\n    '## 🔧 Tool: ',\n    '## ✅ Tool Result:',\n    '## ❌ Tool Result:',\n    '## ✅ Session Complete',\n    '## ❌ Session Failed',\n    '## ❓ Unrecognized Event:',\n    '📄 Raw JSON',\n    '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]',\n    '🤖 AI-Powered Solution Draft',\n    '*This PR was created automatically by the AI issue solver*'\n  ]\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a comment body is system-generated (from interactive mode)\n *\n * @param {string} body - The user's feedback text\n * @returns {string} JSON string ready to write to Claude's stdin\n */\nconst formatFeedbackForClaude = (feedbackText) => {\n  const message = {\n    type: 'user',\n    message: {\n      role: 'user',\n      content: [\n        {\n          type: 'text',\n          text: `[USER FEEDBACK FROM PR COMMENT]\\n\\n${feedbackText}\\n\\n[END OF USER FEEDBACK - Please address this feedback in your current work]`\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  };\n  return JSON.stringify(message);\n};\n\n/**\n * Creates a bidirectional interactive mode handler\n *\n * @param {Object} options - Interval between comment checks (ms)\n * @param {boolean} [options.excludeOwnComments=false] - Exclude comments authored by the same GitHub user that solve runs as (prevents \"talking to yourself\")\n * @returns {Object} Handler object with monitoring methods\n */\nexport const createBidirectionalHandler = (options) => {\n  const {\n    owner,\n    repo,\n    prNumber,\n    $,\n    log,\n    verbose = false,\n    pollInterval = CONFIG.DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL,\n    excludeOwnComments = false\n  } = options;\n  // Resolved lazily on first check, cached for the lifetime of the handler\n  let ownUserLogin = null;\n  let ownUserResolved = false;\n  const resolveOwnUserLogin = async () => {\n    if (ownUserResolved) return ownUserLogin;\n    try {\n      const result = await $`gh api user --jq .login`;\n      ownUserLogin = (result.stdout?.toString() || '').trim() || null;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log(`⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Could not resolve current gh user: ${error.message}`, { verbose: true });\n      }\n      ownUserLogin = null;\n    }\n    ownUserResolved = true;\n    return ownUserLogin;\n  };\n\n  // State tracking for the handler\n  const state = {\n    isMonitoring: false,\n    lastCheckedCommentId: null,\n    lastCheckedTimestamp: null,\n    feedbackQueue: [],\n    pollIntervalId: null,\n    processedCommentIds: new Set(),\n    totalCommentsProcessed: 0,\n    totalFeedbackQueued: 0\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Fetch recent comments from the PR\n   * @returns {Promise<Array>} Array of comment objects\n   * @private\n   */\n  const fetchRecentComments = async () => {\n    if (!prNumber || !owner || !repo) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log('⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Cannot fetch comments - missing PR info', { verbose: true });\n      }\n      return [];\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Fetch comments using gh api with pagination, sorted by created_at desc\n      const result = await $`gh api repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${prNumber}/comments --jq '[.[] | {id: .id, body: .body, created_at: .created_at, user: .user.login}] | sort_by(.created_at) | reverse'`;\n      const comments = JSON.parse(result.stdout.toString());\n      return comments;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log(`⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Failed to fetch comments: ${error.message}`, { verbose: true });\n      }\n      return [];\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Check for new user comments and queue them as feedback\n   * @private\n   */\n  const checkForNewComments = async () => {\n    if (!state.isMonitoring) {\n      return;\n    }\n\n    try {\n      const comments = await fetchRecentComments();\n\n      if (comments.length === 0) {\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Filter for new comments we haven't processed yet\n      for (const comment of comments) {\n        // Skip if already processed\n        if (state.processedCommentIds.has(comment.id)) {\n          continue;\n        }\n\n        // Skip if this is a system-generated comment\n        if (isSystemComment(comment.body)) {\n          state.processedCommentIds.add(comment.id);\n          continue;\n        }\n\n        // This is a new user comment - queue it as feedback\n        if (state.feedbackQueue.length < CONFIG.MAX_QUEUE_SIZE) {\n          state.feedbackQueue.push({\n            id: comment.id,\n            body: comment.body,\n            user: comment.user,\n            created_at: comment.created_at,\n            formattedMessage: formatFeedbackForClaude(comment.body)\n          });\n          state.totalFeedbackQueued++;\n\n          if (verbose) {\n            await log(`📥 Bidirectional mode: Queued feedback from @${comment.user} (comment #${comment.id})`, { verbose: true });\n          }\n        } else {\n          if (verbose) {\n            await log(`⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Feedback queue full, skipping comment #${comment.id}`, { verbose: true });\n          }\n        }\n\n        state.processedCommentIds.add(comment.id);\n        state.totalCommentsProcessed++;\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log(`⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Error checking comments: ${error.message}`, { verbose: true });\n      }\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Start monitoring PR comments for user feedback\n   *\n   * @returns {Promise<void>}\n   */\n  const startMonitoring = async () => {\n    if (state.isMonitoring) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log('ℹ️ Bidirectional mode: Already monitoring', { verbose: true });\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (!prNumber || !owner || !repo) {\n      if (verbose) {\n        await log('⚠️ Bidirectional mode: Cannot start monitoring - Comment ID to mark as processed\n   */\n  const markCommentAsProcessed = (commentId) => {\n    state.processedCommentIds.add(commentId);\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Initialize with existing comment IDs to skip\n   * Call this before startMonitoring() to avoid processing old comments\n   *\n   * @param {Array<number>} commentIds - Array of comment IDs to skip\n   */\n  const initializeWithExistingComments = (commentIds) => {\n    for (const id of commentIds) {\n      state.processedCommentIds.add(id);\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Fetch and mark all existing comments as processed\n   * Call this before startMonitoring() to only get new comments\n   *\n   * @returns {Promise<number>} Number of existing comments marked\n   */\n  const initializeFromCurrentComments = async () => {\n    const comments = await fetchRecentComments();\n    for (const comment of comments) {\n      state.processedCommentIds.add(comment.id);\n    }\n    if (verbose) {\n      await log(`📋 Bidirectional mode: Initialized with ${comments.length} existing comments`, { verbose: true });\n    }\n    return comments.length;\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Get current handler state (for debugging)\n   *\n   * @returns {Object} Current state\n   */\n  const getState = () => ({\n    isMonitoring: state.isMonitoring,\n    feedbackQueueLength: state.feedbackQueue.length,\n    processedCommentCount: state.processedCommentIds.size,\n    totalCommentsProcessed: state.totalCommentsProcessed,\n    totalFeedbackQueued: state.totalFeedbackQueued\n  });\n\n  return {\n    startMonitoring,\n    stopMonitoring,\n    peekFeedback,\n    popFeedback,\n    getAllQueuedFeedback,\n    hasFeedback,\n    getFeedbackCount,\n    clearFeedbackQueue,\n    markCommentAsProcessed,\n    initializeWithExistingComments,\n    initializeFromCurrentComments,\n    getState,\n    // Expose for testing\n    _internal: {\n      checkForNewComments,\n      fetchRecentComments,\n      isSystemComment,\n      formatFeedbackForClaude\n    }\n  };\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if bidirectional interactive mode is supported for the given tool\n *\n * @param {string} tool - Tool name (claude, opencode, codex)\n * @returns {boolean} Whether bidirectional interactive mode is supported\n */\nexport const isBidirectionalModeSupported = (tool) => {\n  // Currently only supported for Claude due to --input-format stream-json support\n  return tool === 'claude';\n};\n\n/**\n * Validate bidirectional interactive mode configuration\n *\n * @param {Object} argv - Parsed command line arguments\n * @param {Function} log - Logging function\n * @returns {Promise<boolean>} Whether configuration is valid\n */\nexport const validateBidirectionalModeConfig = async (argv, log) => {\n  if (!argv.bidirectionalInteractive) {\n    return true; // Not enabled, nothing to validate\n  }\n\n  // Check tool support\n  if (!isBidirectionalModeSupported(argv.tool)) {\n    await log(`⚠️ --bidirectional-interactive is only supported for --tool claude (current: ${argv.tool})`, { level: 'warning' });\n    await log('   Bidirectional interactive mode will be disabled for this session.', { level: 'warning' });\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Bidirectional mode requires interactive-mode to be enabled\n  if (!argv.interactiveMode) {\n    await log('⚠️ --bidirectional-interactive requires --interactive-mode to be enabled', { level: 'warning' });\n    await log('   Enabling --interactive-mode automatically.', { level: 'warning' });\n    argv.interactiveMode = true;\n  }\n\n  await log('🔌 Bidirectional Interactive Mode: ENABLED (experimental)', { level: 'info' });\n  await log('   PR comments will be monitored and queued as feedback for Claude.', { level: 'info' });\n\n  return true;\n};\n\n// Export utilities for testing\nexport const utils = {\n  isSystemComment,\n  formatFeedbackForClaude,\n  CONFIG\n};\n\n// Export all functions\nexport default {\n  createBidirectionalHandler,\n  isBidirectionalModeSupported,\n  validateBidirectionalModeConfig,\n  utils\n};\n",

Timeout Configurations\n\n| Environment Variable                 | Default | Description                                                                   |\n| ------------------------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`   | 60      | Claude CLI timeout in seconds                                                 |\n| `HIVE_MIND_OPENCODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 60      | OpenCode CLI timeout in seconds                                               |\n| `HIVE_MIND_CODEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`    | 60      | Codex CLI timeout in seconds                                                  |\n| `HIVE_MIND_GITHUB_API_DELAY_MS`      | 5000    | Delay between GitHub API calls (ms)                                           |\n| `HIVE_MIND_GITHUB_REPO_DELAY_MS`     | 2000    | Delay between repository operations (ms)                                      |\n| `HIVE_MIND_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS`      | 5000    | Base delay for retry operations (ms)                                          |\n| `HIVE_MIND_RETRY_BACKOFF_DELAY_MS`   | 1000    | Backoff delay for retries (ms)                                                |\n| `HIVE_MIND_RESULT_STREAM_CLOSE_MS`   | 30000   | Timeout (ms) to wait for stream close after result event before force-killing |\n\n### 2. Cache TTL Configurations\n\nThese settings control how long API responses are cached before making a new request.\n\n| Environment Variable               | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                       |\n| ---------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_API_CACHE_TTL_MS`       | 180000  | General API cache TTL in ms (3 minutes). Calling it more frequently may return null values. |\n| `HIVE_MIND_SYSTEM_CACHE_TTL_MS`    | 120000  | System metrics cache TTL in ms (2 minutes). Used for RAM, CPU, and disk space.                                                                                    |\n\n**Note:** The Claude Usage API (`/api/oauth/usage`) is rate-limited more strictly than other APIs. If you experience `null` values in the `/limits` command output, the API call frequency may be too high. The default 10-minute TTL is designed to avoid this issue. See [Issue #1074](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1074) for details.\n\n### 5.2. Claude Code CLI Configurations\n\nThese settings control Claude Code CLI behavior, including output limits and MCP timeouts.\n\n| Environment Variable                    | Default | Description                                                                                           |\n| --------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`         | 64000   | Maximum output tokens for Claude Code CLI responses (also: `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46` | 128000  | Maximum output tokens for Opus 4.6+ (also: `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46`)         |\n| `MCP_TIMEOUT`                           | 900000  | MCP server startup timeout in ms (15 min) (also: `HIVE_MIND_MCP_TIMEOUT`)                             |\n| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`                      | 900000  | MCP tool execution timeout in ms (15 min) (also: `HIVE_MIND_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`)                        |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET_OPUS_46` | 31999   | Default max thinking budget for Opus 4.6+ models                                                      |\n\n**Note:** Claude models support different max output tokens: Opus 4.6 (the default `opus` alias) supports 128K tokens, while Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, and Haiku 4.5 support 64K tokens. The MCP timeouts (15 minutes by default) accommodate long-running Playwright operations. See [Issue #1076](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1076) and [Issue #1066](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1066) for details.\n\n### 6. Playwright MCP\n\nPlaywright MCP (Model Context Protocol) provides browser automation capabilities for Claude Code and Codex, enabling web scraping, UI testing, and interaction with dynamic web pages.\n\n#### Installation\n\n```bash\n# Recommended: Install with memory-safe settings (for servers and Docker)\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\n\n# Minimal installation (for local development)\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless\n```\n\n#### Command-Line Arguments\n\n| Argument                 | Description                                    | Memory Impact                              |\n| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |\n| `--isolated`             | Ephemeral browser contexts (MOST IMPORTANT)    | **HIGH** - Prevents process accumulation   |\n| `--headless`             | Run browser in headless mode                   | **MEDIUM** - Reduces UI memory overhead    |\n| `--browser <type>`       | Browser: chromium, firefox, webkit, msedge     | **VARIES** - WebKit often uses less memory |\n| `--no-sandbox`           | Disable sandbox (controlled environments only) | **LOW** - Reduces memory slightly          |\n| `--timeout-action <ms>`  | Timeout for actions (default: 5000)            | **N/A** - Prevents hung processes          |\n| `--viewport-size <size>` | Set viewport dimensions (e.g., \"1280x720\")     | **LOW** - Affects rendering memory         |\n| `--storage-state <path>` | Load auth state without full profile           | **MEDIUM** - Auth without profile bloat    |\n\n#### Scope Options\n\nClaude Code and Codex do not share MCP registration automatically. Register Playwright MCP in each CLI you expect to use. A working Claude configuration does not make `codex mcp list` show the same server.\n\n| Scope     | Description                     | Config Location                     |\n| --------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |\n| `local`   | Current directory only          | `~/.claude.json` (project-specific) |\n| `project` | Team-shared via version control | `.mcp.json` (project root)          |\n| `user`    | Available globally              | `~/.claude.json` (user section)     |\n\n#### JSON Configuration\n\nClaude Code example (`~/.claude.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"playwright\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"@playwright/mcp@latest\", \"--isolated\", \"--headless\", \"--no-sandbox\", \"--timeout-action=600000\", \"--viewport-size\", \"1920x1080\"],\n      \"env\": {\n        \"PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH\": \"/opt/playwright/browsers\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCodex stores MCP configuration separately. Use the Codex CLI to inspect or register its own Playwright entry:\n\n```bash\n# List configured MCP servers\ncodex mcp list\n\n# Add server\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\n\n# Remove server\ncodex mcp remove playwright\n```\n\n#### MCP Commands\n\n```bash\n# List configured MCP servers\nclaude mcp list\ncodex mcp list\n\n# Get server details\nclaude mcp get playwright\n\n# Remove server\nclaude mcp remove playwright\ncodex mcp remove playwright\n```\n\n#### Best Practices\n\n1. **Always use `--isolated` mode** - Prevents Chrome process accumulation and memory leaks\n2. **Pin to a specific version** - Use `@playwright/mcp@0.0.49` instead of `@latest` for stability\n3. **Use `--headless` for servers** - Reduces memory overhead in CI/CD and production environments\n4. **Restart Claude Code periodically** - For long-running sessions to clear accumulated browser resources\n\nFor comprehensive configuration options, troubleshooting, and advanced use cases, see the detailed guide:\n[Playwright MCP Configuration Guide](./case-studies/issue-837-playwright-mcp-chrome-leak/04-CLAUDE-PLAYWRIGHT-MCP-CONFIGURATION.md)\n\n---\n\n## Command-Line Options\n\n### solve Options\n\n```bash\nsolve <issue-url> [2026-04-18T17:43:18.405Z] [INFO]   ✅ Found pull request #843: "Implement bidirectional interactive mode for real-time PR feedback"
[2026-04-18T17:43:19.007Z] [STDOUT] ## Summary

This PR implements the **bidirectional interactive mode** feature requested in issue #817, with a composable 3-option design per the latest PR feedback.

### New CLI options (all EXPERIMENTAL, all default off)

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--accept-incomming-comments-as-input` | Accept new PR/issue comments as input for Claude during execution. System comments generated by solve itself are excluded automatically. Does **not** require `--interactive-mode`. Only supported for `--tool claude`. |
| `--exclude-all-own-incomming-comments-from-input` | When combined with the flag above, also exclude comments authored by the same GitHub user that solve runs as (prevents self-talk during testing). |
| `--bidirectional-interactive-mode` | Convenience composite flag that turns on all three: `--interactive-mode`, `--accept-incomming-comments-as-input`, and `--exclude-all-own-incomming-comments-from-input`. |

These are composable: the user can still run `--interactive-mode --accept-incomming-comments-as-input` without `--exclude-all-own-...` so "talking to yourself" from the same GitHub user continues to work for manual testing.

### Behaviour

1. Polls new PR comments at a 15s interval while Claude is running.
2. Skips system-generated comments (session start/stop, tool events, AI-PR signatures, etc.).
3. Optionally skips comments authored by the same GitHub user that solve runs as (resolved lazily via `gh api user --jq .login`).
4. Formats each remaining comment into Claude's `--input-format stream-json` payload and queues it.
5. Surfaces queued feedback in the execution result for downstream handling.

All three flags default to `false`; previous logic is untouched unless a flag is explicitly passed.

### Files changed

- `src/bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs` - new module: `createBidirectionalHandler`, `isSystemComment`, `formatFeedbackForClaude`, `validateBidirectionalModeConfig`, `isBidirectionalModeSupported`. Supports `excludeOwnComments` with cached `gh api user` lookup.
- `src/claude.lib.mjs` - calls `validateBidirectionalModeConfig`, starts the handler when `acceptIncommingCommentsAsInput` is set, flushes the queue on exit, returns `queuedFeedback` on every exit path.
- `src/solve.config.lib.mjs` - registers the three new options in `SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS`.
- `src/hive.config.lib.mjs` - options auto-propagate via `SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS` (no manual additions needed).
- `tests/test-bidirectional-interactive.mjs` - 31 tests covering validation, the composite flag, and `excludeOwnComments` true/false paths.

### Usage examples

```bash
# Full bidirectional experience (interactive + accept + exclude-own)
solve https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123 --bidirectional-interactive-mode

# Accept incoming comments in interactive mode without excluding your own user
# (useful when testing against your own account)
solve https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123 \
  --interactive-mode \
  --accept-incomming-comments-as-input

# Use from hive (auto-forwarded via SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS)
hive https://github.com/owner/repo --bidirectional-interactive-mode
```
